title: A finite Behenian star register could use repeated exact plant forms as cross-row links
summary: Source-only proposal: repeated exact plant strings in a complete fifteen-star roster may form a relational network, with flower/root qualifiers preserved.
mechanism: A fifteen-row fixed-star register carries explicit stone and plant bundles. Repeated plant strings are relational links between rows, while source-preserved part qualifiers (flowers/root) remain distinct until independently justified.
target_endpoint: A future comparison against an already admitted fifteen-group object; no target body, key, or mapping was inspected for this card.

two_readings.name: shared-material network
two_readings.claim: Repeated exact forms such as Mugwort link several distinct star rows; flowers of Perwinckle and the root of Mandrake retain narrower part roles.
consequences: A candidate fifteen-group reading must show repeated units linking multiple distinct positions, not merely fifteen distinct labels.
A candidate must preserve the source's qualifier contrast unless an independent rule collapses it.

two_readings.name: independent row vocabulary
two_readings.claim: Each row is an independent bundle and repeated plant words are ordinary lexical reuse without a cross-row relation.
consequences: Repeated units need not connect corresponding positions or carry a shared network role.
Flowers/root qualifiers may be ordinary descriptive detail rather than distinct coded nodes.

smallest_distinguishing_observation: Before assigning meanings, compare a source-frozen fifteen-position candidate for exact repeated-form links across distinct positions and for preserved part qualifiers. A stable multi-row repeat network supports the first mechanism; no such network or systematic loss of qualifiers leaves the rival viable.
strongest_failure: Agrippa's 1651 English witness may copy or normalize an older star list, and the admitted target may lack independently established fifteen-row boundaries. Repeated plants could therefore be source-specific coincidence or transcriptional reuse.
falsifier: Reject this card if every putative repeated form occurs only within one position, or if the only network appears after modern synonymy and arbitrary plant-part collapsing.
assumption_costs: The source roster is historically relevant to the target's genre.
A target fifteen-group unit and ordering can be fixed without choosing meanings.
Exact visual forms can be compared without importing English glosses.
review_note: The repeated-incidence network is a source-derived constraint, not evidence that any target form means Mugwort or Mandrake.
